purpose: Pentosan polysulfate is used to relieve the bladder pain and discomfort caused by a condition called interstitial cystitis, sometimes called painful bladder syndrome. It helps reduce the burning, pressure, and frequent need to urinate that comes with this condition. It is the only oral pill approved specifically for this condition.
how_it_works: The inside lining of your bladder has a protective coating, and in interstitial cystitis, that coating is damaged or too thin. Pentosan polysulfate works by helping to repair and restore that protective lining in your bladder. Think of it like a bandage for the inside of your bladder, which helps reduce irritation and pain.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include hair loss (usually mild and often reversible), nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, and headache. Some people may notice bruising more easily or have minor bleeding issues since the medication has mild blood-thinning effects.
warnings: Important: Long-term use of this medication has been linked to a rare but serious eye condition called pigmentary maculopathy, which can affect your central vision. You should have regular eye exams while taking this medication and report any vision changes to your doctor right away. Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners, aspirin, or anti-inflammatory medications, as the combination may increase bleeding risk. Do not take this medication if you are allergic to it or are pregnant without consulting your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is one 100 mg capsule taken three times a day, about 1 hour before meals or 2 hours after meals, with a full glass of water. It can take 3 to 6 months before you notice significant improvement in your symptoms, so it is important to keep taking it as directed even if you do not feel better right away.
